headline: Congress used a resolution to cancel a Social Security Administration rule that would have sent some beneficiaries' names to the national gun background check system.
what_it_does: The Social Security Administration finalized a rule in December 2016 to give the National Instant Criminal History Background Check System the names of certain people. Those people receive benefit payments through a representative payee because they were found mentally incapable of managing their own money. This joint resolution cancels that rule, so it does not take effect. Current law on who may buy, sell, or possess firearms stays the same.

who_it_affects.group: Social Security beneficiaries who have a representative payee
who_it_affects.how: Their names will not be sent to the background check system under the canceled rule.

who_it_affects.group: People who buy or transfer firearms
who_it_affects.how: Background checks will not include names from this rule, so the process stays as it was under existing law.
It cannot carry out the canceled rule and must follow the rules that were in place before it.

when_it_takes_effect: The cancellation took effect when the President signed it into law on February 28, 2017.
